name: Sketchlight
tagline: Turn a photo into lines and trace it on paper with your iPhone or iPad — draw someone you love and give it as a gift.
storage_summary: Your photos, sketches, projects, finished drawings, recordings and settings are stored only on your iPhone or iPad. Sketchlight has no account and no server of its own. Turning a photo into lines, finding the subject and finding your sheet of paper all run on your device, and the camera view never leaves it. Usage events go to Google Analytics for Firebase so we can fix problems and improve the app; only if you allow tracking, they are also used to measure our Google Ads campaigns.
nothing_sent_detail: Your photos, the camera view, your drawings and anything you type are never sent to us or to Google Analytics.

apple_storekit.name: Apple (App Store purchases)
apple_storekit.purpose: Processes the Sketchlight Pro subscription or one-time purchase and verifies that it is active.
apple_storekit.data: your purchase receipt, handled by Apple (we never see your payment details, Apple Account or name)

firebase.name: Google Analytics for Firebase
firebase.purpose: Measures how the app is used (for example whether a tracing session was started or the upgrade screen was opened) so we can fix problems and improve the app, and — only if you allow tracking — measures whether our Google Ads campaigns led to the app being installed or used, using Google's on-device measurement.
firebase.data: a small set of usage events and their settings (never your photos, drawings or anything you type), an app-instance identifier, app version, device model, OS version, locale, approximate region derived from your IP address, and purchase events (product and result); if you allow tracking in the App Tracking Transparency prompt, your advertising identifier (IDFA)

data_sent.what: Usage events and purchase events (never your photos, drawings or anything you type), app-instance identifier, app and device info, locale, approximate region; the advertising identifier (IDFA) only if you allow tracking
data_sent.why: Understand how the app is used, fix problems, improve the app and, only with your permission, measure our Google Ads campaigns
Confirm that your Sketchlight Pro purchase is active

stored_on_device: The photos you choose, the sketches made from them, and your tracing projects with their position and opacity.
Photos of your finished drawings and any tracing recordings you make.
Your favorite templates, lesson progress, daily challenge streak and settings such as appearance, accent color and reminder time.
The template library and lessons are built into the app, so they work without an internet connection.
Delete a project or a drawing at any time in My Art, or delete everything by deleting the app.
not_collected: Your name, email address or any account, because Sketchlight has no sign-in.
Your photos, the camera view or your drawings — they never leave your device unless you share them yourself.
Your location, contacts or browsing history.
Payment details — Sketchlight Pro is bought through Apple, and we never see your card, Apple Account or name.

permissions.name: Camera
permissions.why: to show your picture over the paper so you can trace it, and to photograph your finished drawing. The camera view stays on your device and is never uploaded. You can say no and trace in Light Box mode instead.

permissions.name: Photos (add only)
permissions.why: to save your sketches and drawings to your photo library when you tap Save to Photos. Choosing a photo uses the system photo picker, so Sketchlight never sees the rest of your library.

permissions.name: Notifications
permissions.why: to send the daily challenge reminder at the time you choose. Nothing leaves your device for this.

permissions.name: Tracking (App Tracking Transparency)
permissions.why: asked once after onboarding. If you allow it, your advertising identifier (IDFA) is used only to measure whether our Google Ads campaigns brought you to Sketchlight. If you decline, nothing changes in the app and the IDFA is never read.

your_controls: **Delete a project or a drawing** in **My Art**, or delete everything by deleting the app — your work lives only on your device.
**Turn camera, photo saving or notifications off or on** in iOS Settings → Sketchlight.
**Turn the daily reminder off** in **Settings → Daily challenge** in the app.
**Manage or cancel your subscription** in iOS Settings → your name → Subscriptions.
**Allow or stop tracking** at any time in iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Tracking → Sketchlight.

subscription.restore_location: on the Sketchlight Pro screen, or in Settings

support_faq.q: How do I trace with my phone?
support_faq.a: Pick a template or a photo, then tap **Trace**. Prop your phone on a stand or a stack of books above your paper, line up the picture, tap **Lock**, and trace what you see on the screen onto the paper.

support_faq.q: I don't have a stand. Can I still trace?
support_faq.a: Yes. Switch to **Light Box** in the trace screen, lay a thin sheet of paper on the screen and trace the picture through it.
Open iOS **Settings → Sketchlight** and turn on **Camera**. You can also trace in **Light Box** mode without the camera.

support_faq.q: How do I restore my purchase?
support_faq.a: Open the **Sketchlight Pro** screen or **Settings** in the app and tap **Restore Purchases**, signed in with the same Apple Account you bought with.

support_faq.q: How do I delete my data?
support_faq.a: Delete projects and drawings in **My Art**, or delete the app. Your work lives only on your device, so this removes it completely.

tracking_detail: After you finish the welcome screens, iOS asks whether Sketchlight may track you (App Tracking Transparency). We advertise Sketchlight with Google Ads. Only if you tap **Allow**, Google Analytics for Firebase receives your device's advertising identifier (IDFA), and app installs, the start of a free trial and Sketchlight Pro purchases (product and price) are shared with Google Ads so we can tell which of our ads brought new users. Google also uses on-device conversion measurement, which matches an ad to an install on your iPhone or iPad without sending your name, email or phone number. If you tap **Ask App Not to Track**, no IDFA is collected; Apple's SKAdNetwork may still tell Google Ads that an ad led to an install, without identifying you or your device. You can change this any time in iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Tracking. Your photos, the camera view and your drawings are never used for this.
